Exercise 3. Use R to simulate and plot some data from simple ARMA models.

1. Generate data from an AR(1) model with ϕ1 = 0.6 and σ2 = 1. The process starts with y1 = 0. Try several values of ϕ1.

```{r}
#rm(list = ls())
library(fable)
library(tsibble)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(123)

y <- numeric (100)
e <- rnorm (100)
phi <- 0.6

for (i in 2:100){
  y[i] <- phi *y[i -1] + e[i]
  }

sim <- tsibble ( idx = seq_len (100) , y = y, index = idx )


```

2. Produce a time plot for the series. How does the plot change as you change ϕ1?

```{r}

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(sim, aes(x = idx, y = y)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "AR(1) Model with phi = 0.6",
       x = "Time", y = "y") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "blue", linetype = 2)


```

3. Write your own code to generate data from an MA(1) model with θ1 = 0.6 and σ2 = 1.

```{r}
set.seed(12)

Y <- numeric (100)
eps <- rnorm (100)
theta <- 0.6

for (i in 2:100){
  Y[i] <- theta *eps[i-1] + eps[i]
  }

sim_ma1 <- tsibble ( idx = seq_len (100) , y = Y, index = idx )

```

4. Produce a time plot for the series. How does the plot change as you change θ1?

```{r}
ggplot(sim_ma1, aes(x = idx, y = y)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "MA(1) Model with theta = 0.6",
       x = "Time", y = "y") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "green", linetype = 2)


```

5. Generate data from an ARMA(1,1) model with ϕ1 = 0.6, θ1 = 0.6 and σ2 = 1.

```{r}

set.seed(21)

Y <- numeric(100)
eps <- rnorm(100)
phi <- 0.6
theta <- 0.6

for (i in 2:100) {
  Y[i] <- phi * Y[i-1] + eps[i] + theta * eps[i-1]
}

sim_arma11 <- tsibble(idx = seq_len(100), y = Y, index = idx)


ggplot(sim_arma11, aes(x = idx, y = y)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "ARMA(1,1) Model",
       x = "Time", y = "Y") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "blue", linetype = 2)


```

6. Generate data from an AR(2) model with ϕ1 =−0.8, ϕ2 = 0.3 and σ2 = 1. Explain why this series appears not-stationary.

```{r}


set.seed(123)

Y <- numeric(100)
eps <- rnorm(100)
phi1 <- -0.8
phi2 <- 0.3

for (i in 3:100) {
  Y[i] <- phi1 * Y[i-1] + phi2 * Y[i-2] + eps[i]
}

sim_ar2 <- tsibble(idx = seq_len(100), y = Y, index = idx)


ggplot(sim_ar2, aes(x = idx, y = y)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "AR(2) Model",
       x = "Time", y = "Y") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "blue", linetype = 2)



```

7. Plot the latter two series and compare them.

```{r}


data_arma11 <- as.data.frame(sim_arma11)
data_ar2 <- as.data.frame(sim_ar2)

data_arma11$model <- "ARMA(1,1)"
data_ar2$model <- "AR(2)"

both_series <- bind_rows(data_arma11, data_ar2)

ggplot(both_series, aes(x = idx, y = y)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "ARMA(1,1) vs AR(2)",
    x = "Time",
    y = "Y"
  )

```
